item.text: {"text":"Recent work supports separating recency, sequence order, and noisy history effects. [CETRec (2025)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.03047) distinguishes absolute order—how recently an interaction occurred—from relative order between interactions, and proposes counterfactual tuning to improve temporal sensitivity. [CoDeR (AAAI 2025)](https://ojs.aaai.org/index.php/AAAI/article/view/33379) models demand shifts amid noisy histories; its causal interpretation depends on its assumptions. [Disentangling User and Item Sequence Patterns (RecSys 2025)](https://researchportal.helsinki.fi/en/publications/disentangling-user-and-item-sequence-patterns-in-sequential-recom/) compares random and item-availability-constrained shuffling, showing that apparent sequential signal can originate from item availability as well as user behavior. [Semantically Consistent Contrastive Learning (2025)](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S089360802500070X) warns that random cropping, masking, and reordering can change sequence semantics.\n\nSuggested diagnostic synthesis: mask recent events, remove repeated-interest evidence, and shuffle order as separate interventions. Define repeated interests using observable item recurrence or title/description similarity; these are proxies, not observed intent. Compare targeted removals against equal-size random removals matched on position and item popularity where feasible; preserve the item multiset for order probes, and distinguish shuffling older context from moving the latest item. Measure paired target-rank changes, score margins, and top-10 overlap using fixed candidates and repeated control draws. These assess model dependence, not causal user preferences. [A 2026 temporal-attribution benchmark](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.27201) reports that raw attention is unreliable as a faithfulness explanation. Connect diagnostic signatures to candidate changes in sequence encoding, recency weighting, or training objectives, then test whether those changes improve category-specific validation HR@10 and the four-category macro average. Probe sensitivity alone does not establish recommendation quality."}
